title: Post with a plan, stay safe, and measure what works

say: Post with a plan, stay safe, and measure what works.
This is the video for module three of Personal Branding and Online Presence.
Content pillars are the three or four main topics you post about again and again. Without them, posting becomes random, and random posting confuses people about what you do.
Here are four kinds that work for most people. Imagine a caterer.

panel.heading: Four kinds of pillar
items: Teach: help people with what you know
Show the work: process and result
Proof: results and reviews
Personal and values: let people know you

say: Your goal is to be easy to find for work, and hard to target for harm. Here are three scams that target public profiles.

cards.d: A message asks you to forward a code sent by mistake. It is your login code. Never share it.
Someone copies your name and photo and asks your customers to pay. Warn them you use one number.
Screenshots or SMS that look like credit alerts. Confirm in your own bank or wallet app.

say: Code theft. A message, often from a friend's hacked account, asks you to forward a code sent by mistake. It is your login code. Never share it.

say: A client's name, face, house, chat or result belongs to her. Posting them without asking can embarrass her and break her trust.

panel.heading: Ask before you share
right: No name, as the client asked
Street and family photo cropped out

say: For example, Bisi is an interior decorator in Ibadan. A happy client sent photos of her finished living room. Bisi asked in writing if she could share two photos and one line from her message.
The client agreed, but asked that her name is not used. Bisi cropped out a family portrait and a window showing the street, and saved the permission in a folder called Permissions.

panel.heading: Ask before you share
right: No name, as the client asked
Street and family photo cropped out

say: Before you post, check five things. No home address or routine. No children's school details. No ID or card numbers. Client permission obtained. And every claim is true.

Nigeria has the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023. For a small business, that means collect only the customer data you need, keep it secure, and never add people to broadcast lists without their agreement.

say: How do you know your brand is working? By what happens because of it. Every time someone new contacts you, ask politely how they heard about you.

panel.heading: Halima's monthly review
items: Ask every new contact: how did you hear of me?
Log date, source, request and result
Month one: 7 enquiries, 3 paying clients
Decide: keep, change or stop

say: Write it in a simple enquiry log: the date, the source, what they wanted, and the result.

say: So she kept Status at 4 updates a week and added a clear booking line to her Instagram tips. Give any change at least four weeks before you judge it, and never buy followers.

say: Your practice. Choose three or four pillars and a weekly rhythm you can keep. Batch your first four posts in one sitting. Review your WhatsApp privacy settings. Then start your enquiry log and your Permissions folder.
